newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM says pushing for rapid cabinet changes.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM says pushing for rapid cabinet changes.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Tuesday that he will push for the rapid reconstruction of the cabinet, in an attempt to help stifle political uncertainty which has hit the crown hard in recent weeks.

"I agreed with President (Vaclav) Havel on how to proceed further. I consider it important for fast negotiations for finalising the coalition talks...finalising the reconstruction of the government," he said after a meeting with Havel.
A first round of talks between Czech coalition parties on a cabinet reshuffle ended inconclusively on Monday, two days after the finance and interior ministers resigned.
Klaus, who leads the senior Civic Democratic Party (ODS), began discussing the extent of the shake-up with coalition partners after the two ministers, both from the ODS, stepped down on Saturday.

The leaders agreed to change the cabinet last week in response to a sharp drop in the centre-right government's approval ratings amid an economic downturn and a widespread feeling that financial crime is pervasive. But Monday's failed meeting suggested agreement on the share-out of ministerial posts reshuffle would be difficult.
Klaus did not disclose what he and Havel had agreed to.
